questions.q: What does role-based prompting change, according to this lesson?
options: Vocabulary, priorities, and depth — not just tone
Nothing measurable — it is purely cosmetic
Only the length of the response
Only the formatting of the output, nothing else
questions.explain: Assigning a role shifts what the model treats as important and how deeply it explores a given point, not just the surface tone of the reply.

questions.q: In the SQL vs. NoSQL example, why do the startup CTO, database architect, and freelancer give different answers?
options: Because the question itself changes slightly for each role
Because only one of the three roles is capable of answering the question correctly
Because each role has a different idea of what matters most, producing legitimately different, defensible answers
Because two of the three roles are deliberately given wrong information
questions.explain: Each role weighs different priorities — time-to-market, consistency guarantees, or cost — leading to different but all defensible answers.

questions.q: How does this lesson distinguish a per-request role from a system prompt's role field?
options: They are described as being exactly identical in every way
A per-request role is layered on for one specific task without changing the assistant's standing identity elsewhere
A system prompt role only applies to coding tasks
A per-request role can only be used once per account, ever
questions.explain: The system prompt's role sets a standing identity for the whole conversation, while a per-request role applies just to a single task.

questions.q: What is the problem with a vague role instruction like "Act like a doctor"?
options: It automatically overrides the system prompt
The model will refuse to respond to any medical question
It is too long for the model to process
It risks a shallow, stereotyped answer because it gives the model a costume, not real expertise
questions.explain: A vague, one-word role gives the model a surface persona without specifying the professional context, audience, or communication style needed for real expertise.

questions.q: What three things does a well-specified role prompt include, according to this lesson's pediatrician example?
options: The exact word count, font, and color of the response
Three unrelated follow-up questions to ask afterward
Who the expert is, who the answer is for, and how it should communicate
The model's temperature, top-p, and max token settings
questions.explain: "A board-certified pediatrician explaining a fever to a worried parent, in plain, reassuring language" specifies who, the audience, and the communication style.
